personal.name: Francesco Coccia
personal.title: Cyber Security Analyst | Penetration Tester | Secure Software Engineer

summary: Cyber security professional with 4 years of enterprise software engineering experience, currently completing an NCSC-certified MSc in Computer Forensics and Cyber Security at the University of Greenwich. I bring hands-on expertise in penetration testing, digital forensics, and secure API development — combined with real production scars from hardening .NET 8 and Ruby on Rails applications across multi-tenant SaaS environments. I think like an attacker, build like an engineer.

bullets: Architecting the full data security strategy for an early-stage UK platform handling sensitive founder, developer, and startup data — building compliance posture from zero.
Designing and enforcing internal access controls, data handling policies, and security governance frameworks aligned with UK GDPR and ISO 27001.
Running continuous security reviews and vulnerability assessments, pressure-testing infrastructure assumptions with the Tech Lead before risks reach production.
Embedding security-by-design thinking across product decisions — advising on data flows, third-party integrations, and cloud config to shrink the attack surface.
Delivered 3 major releases of an enterprise HCM/ERP SaaS platform serving 500+ corporate clients, enforcing secure coding standards, input validation, and RBAC throughout.
Designed SQL Server schemas with least-privilege access, parameterised queries, and audit logging — reducing injection risk surface by ~90% across 12 integrated modules.
Built RESTful API integrations with OAuth2 and API key authentication across 8 third-party SaaS platforms.
Conducted security-aware code reviews catching 4–6 access control issues per release cycle.
Built 6 full-stack web applications with secure authentication, session management, and authorisation flows following OWASP principles.
Mitigated XSS and SQL injection vulnerabilities, resolving 20+ security-related bugs including authentication edge cases and API exposure issues.
